need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio has no managed OAuth app for ServiceNow, so you must supply your own client ID and secret. In practice the OAuth client is created in each customer's instance.

prerequisites.title: Admin access on the instance

steps.title: Create OAuth client in Application Registry
steps.detail: A customer admin goes to System OAuth > Application Registry, creates the OAuth app and sets it active. The client ID is auto-generated.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with the client ID and secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into the OAuth app.

steps.title: Draft customer setup instructions
steps.detail: Write a short guide for customer admins covering roles, grant type and redirect URI.

steps.title: Prepare certification documents
steps.detail: Draft the Design Document, Test Plan and Installation Guide, plus listing text.

steps.title: Join Build Partner Program and submit
steps.detail: Complete partner enrollment, record demo videos and submit the app and listing.

traps.title: No managed app in Composio
traps.detail: You cannot prototype with a Composio-managed ServiceNow app; bring your own credentials from the start.

traps.title: Setup is per customer instance
traps.detail: Each customer's admin must create the OAuth client on their instance with the right role.

traps.title: Self-signed certificates fail
traps.detail: The OAuth client refuses endpoints with self-signed certificates.

traps.title: Store review timing is a typical value
traps.detail: The 3-5 weeks is typical; it can be days or longer than 5 weeks.

blockers.symptom: Cannot open or edit Application Registry

blockers.symptom: OAuth connection to an endpoint is rejected

blockers.what_to_do: Use a certificate from a trusted authority.
